title: Lesson 5: Je cherche le métro
description: A short exchange for asking directions, using chercher, apologizing politely, and following simple street directions.

notes.1: French does not have a separate verb form to express a present continuous action, such as I am looking. Instead, you use the simple form, I look, which makes life much easier.
notes.2: Le Métropolitain, known universally as le métro, is the underground railway system, or subway, of major cities such as Paris, Marseille, or Lyon. The word is also used to refer to a specific station: le métro Châtelet, the Châtelet metro station, as well as to the train itself. You can also ask for une station de métro, a metro station.
notes.3: As we will see throughout this course, a substantial portion of English vocabulary is derived from French. While désolé is the root of desolate and desolation, it is an ordinary, everyday word equivalent to sorry: Je suis désolé, I'm sorry.
notes.4: French people use madame and monsieur a lot when addressing strangers. This is not as formal as it might sound in English, which lacks a convenient, polite way of catching someone's attention.
notes.5: Une ville means a city or a town. French makes no difference between the two.
notes.6: Voilà is the companion word to voici. In principle, we use voici to designate something or someone located close to us, like here is or here are, and voilà for something farther away, like there is or there are. In practice, voilà is used in both instances.

lines.french: Excusez-moi, je cherche le métro Saint-Michel.
lines.english: Excuse me, I'm looking for the Saint-Michel metro station.

lines.french: Désolée, madame, je ne suis pas d'ici.
lines.english: Sorry, madam, I'm not from here.

lines.french: Mais attendez une minute, j'ai un plan de la ville.
parts: Mais attendez une minute, j'ai un plan de la ville
lines.english: But wait a minute, I have a map of the city.

lines.french: Voilà : traversez le boulevard et tournez à gauche à la fontaine.
parts: : traversez le boulevard et tournez à gauche à la fontaine.
lines.english: Here we are: cross the boulevard and turn left at the fountain.
Thanks very much for your help!

tests.title: Exercice 1 - Traduisez
tests.instructions: Listen, then rebuild the French sentence in order.

items.english: Excuse me, I'm looking for the metro station.
I'm sorry, I'm not from here.
Thanks very much for your help.

tests.title: Exercice 2 - Complétez
tests.subtitle: Exercise 2 - Fill in the missing words
tests.instructions: Each dot represents a character, which can be a letter, an apostrophe, a hyphen, etc.

items.english: Cross the boulevard and turn left at the fountain.
Are you looking for the metro station?
